newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Kuchma sees faster Ukraine reforms after Lazarenko.
newsitem.headline: Kuchma sees faster Ukraine reforms after Lazarenko.

text.p: Ukraine President Leonid Kuchma said on Wednesday after accepting his prime minister's resignation that reforms in the country would now move faster.
"Kuchma said a new phase in the activity of the government had begun and that reforms would now be carried out more actively," said presidential spokesman Dmytro Markov.
Markov said he was quoting what Kuchma had told the visiting deputy head of Germany's Christian Democrat party.
"Government itself should be restructured as well," said Kuchma, who earlier signed a decree accepting the resignation of premier Pavlo Lazarenko.
Kuchma has said the number of government officials should be reduced by a third to make their work more efficient and to get economic reforms moving faster.

The International Monetary Fund warned after parliament failed to pass this year's budget until June 27 that Ukraine may have to wait for a $2.5 to $3 billion, three-year loan meant for countries undertaking structural reforms.
The IMF said a second, interim standby deal may be offered instead.
An IMF mission is in Ukraine and the Economy Ministry said on Wednesday that talks were continuing on whether the Extended Fund Facility loan could be agreed.
Kuchma had come under increasing pressure from Western and Ukrainian officials to remove Lazarenko, accused of being partly to blame for sluggish reforms especially in privatisation.
